raw_graphql_pull_request.body: # [metrics] Add cache eviction lifetime/frequency metrics (L1 + L2) ## Motivation SGLang's radix / HiCache eviction is purely capacity-driven (LRU/LFU/FIFO/SLRU/…). There is currently **no** notion of *how long a cache entry lives*, *whether it can survive 1 hour*, or *how often eviction happens*. Operators cannot answer these basic capacity questions today, so "the hit rate is low" can only be guessed at. The data already exists on every `TreeNode` (`creation_time`, `last_access_time`, `hit_count`), and the evicted node is in hand inside `evict()` — this PR simply records it at the moment of eviction. In addition, the L2 (host / CPU DRAM) eviction path (`evict_host`) previously had **no metrics at all**, so the host tier was a complete blind spot. This is observability only: **no eviction/routing behavior is changed.** ## Modifications New metrics on `RadixCacheMetricsCollector` (gated by `--enable-metrics`): Histograms: - `sglang:cache_eviction_age_seconds` — age (`now - creation_time`) of an L1 (GPU) entry at eviction; p50/p90 directly answer "how long does cache live". Buckets span 1s..7200s with a **3600s bucket** so the "1 hour" question is directly readable. - `sglang:cache_eviction_idle_seconds` — idle time (`now - last_access_time`) at eviction. - `sglang:cache_eviction_reuses` — how many times an entry was reused before eviction. (Named `reuses`, not `hit_count`, so the histogram base name does not collide with the reserved `_count` suffix.) - `sglang:hicache_host_eviction_age_seconds` — L2 (host) entry age at eviction. Counters: - `sglang:cache_eviction_events_total` — number of eviction passes; `rate(...)` answers "how often does eviction happen". - `sglang:hicache_host_evicted_tokens_total` — tokens evicted from the L2 host cache. Buckets are configurable via `SGLANG_BUCKET_CACHE_AGE` / `SGLANG_BUCKET_CACHE_REUSES`. Instrumentation (records only when an entry actually leaves the tier; no behavior change): - `RadixCache.evict()` — L1, non-HiCache deployments (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py`). - `HiRadixCache.evict()` — L1 under HiCache (separate override; a `write_back` demotion to host is treated as "left L1", so age = GPU residency) (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py`). - `HiRadixCache.evict_host()` — L2 true end-of-life (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py`). - New collector fields + `observe_eviction_age()`, `increment_eviction_events()`, `increment_host_eviction_num_tokens()`, `observe_host_eviction_age()` (`python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py`). Files: - `python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py` - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py` ## Coverage / limitations Covers `RadixCache` and `HiRadixCache` (and `LMCRadixCache`, which calls `super().evict()`). The other tree caches — `UnifiedRadixCache`, `SWARadixCache`, `MambaRadixCache`, `HiMambaRadixCache`, `RadixCacheCpp` — each have their own `evict()` and are intentionally left as follow-up. The `cache_type` label makes any uninstrumented cache obvious (no series), so this is safe incremental coverage. ## Test process (verified on a live deployment) - Engine: `sglang` v0.5.12 (cu129), model **MiniMax-M2.7**, `tp=8/ep=8` on 8×GPU. - Flags: `--enable-metrics --enable-hierarchical-cache` (HiCache, `write_back`), `--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy best_effort`. - To force eviction quickly the server was relaunched with a deliberately small cache: `--hicache-size 2` (≈2 GB host per rank) and `--max-total-tokens 40000` (tiny GPU KV pool). This is a test knob only; the metrics themselves are unconditional. - Workload: ~290 `/generate` requests — 20 prompts sent twice (to create cache *hits* so `reuses` is non-zero), then 250 distinct ~1.4k-token prompts to overflow both the GPU KV pool (→ L1 eviction / demotion) and the 2 GB host cache (→ L2 `evict_host`). - Then `curl localhost:30000/metrics`. Before the patch, none of the metric names below existed in `/metrics` (`grep -c cache_eviction_age|...|hicache_host_evicted_tokens = 0`). ## Key logs / sample output (real, captured after the workload) ``` # L1 (GPU) entry lifetime at eviction — note the 3600s ("1 hour") bucket is present sglang:cache_eviction_age_seconds_bucket{cache_type="HiRadixCache",le="1.0"} 744 sglang:cache_eviction_age_seconds_bucket{cache_type="HiRadixCache",le="10.0"} 4256 sglang:cache_eviction_age_seconds_bucket{cache_type="HiRadixCache",le="3600.0"} 4280 sglang:cache_eviction_age_seconds_count{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 4280 sglang:cache_eviction_age_seconds_sum{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 8608.23 # idle time before eviction sglang:cache_eviction_idle_seconds_count{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 4280 sglang:cache_eviction_idle_seconds_sum{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 7059.88 # reuse (hit) count before eviction — non-zero thanks to the repeated prompts sglang:cache_eviction_reuses_bucket{cache_type="HiRadixCache",le="1.0"} 1904 sglang:cache_eviction_reuses_bucket{cache_type="HiRadixCache",le="2.0"} 3928 sglang:cache_eviction_reuses_count{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 4280 sglang:cache_eviction_reuses_sum{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 7976 # how often eviction happens sglang:cache_eviction_events_total{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 328 # L2 (host) tier — previously had NO metrics at all sglang:hicache_host_evicted_tokens_total{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 2112616 sglang:hicache_host_eviction_age_seconds_count{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 3928 sglang:hicache_host_eviction_age_seconds_sum{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 13764.54 ``` Example query — "p90 lifetime of an L1 cache entry": ``` histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(sglang:cache_eviction_age_seconds_bucket[5m]))) ``` (In this stress run the cache was intentionally tiny, so entries lived only a few seconds on average — `age_sum/age_count ≈ 2 s`. On a normally-sized cache these histograms are what tells you whether your KV cache actually survives an hour.) ## Checklist - [x] Start a server with `--enable-metrics`, drive eviction, attach a `curl /metrics` sample (above). - [x] Verified both L1 (`RadixCache`/`HiRadixCache.evict`) and L2 (`evict_host`) paths emit under HiCache (`cache_type="HiRadixCache"`). - [ ] Add unit tests for the new collector methods. > related: #24656 (measurement prerequisite for TTL), #26974 (complementary; this is > lifetime, not transfer speed) --- ## PR series / dependencies This is one of four independent observability PRs (a "cache observability" series). **None of them depend on each other to build or merge**, and they can be merged in any order: - `[router] cache-aware decision observability` (gateway / Rust) - `[metrics] cache eviction lifetime/frequency (L1+L2)` (engine / Python) - `[metrics] radix cache size gauges` (engine / Python) - `[tracing] per-request cache-match snapshot` (engine / Python) Notes: - The two `[metrics]` engine PRs touch `metrics_collector.py` and `radix_cache.py` in **different regions**; whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase. - The `[tracing]` per-request `cache_match` event is designed to **correlate** with the gateway routing span (the `[router]` PR) via the W3C `trace_id`, but it is fully functional on its own. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #29177971171](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29177971171) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #29177971139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29177971139)

Cache-observability series (independent, any merge order):
- #28509 `[router]` cache-aware decision observability (gateway/Rust)
- #28507 `[metrics]` cache eviction lifetime/frequency L1+L2 (engine)
- #28508 `[metrics]` radix cache size gauges (engine)
- #28510 `[tracing]` per-request cache-match snapshot (engine)

Only coupling: #28507 and #28508 edit `metrics_collector.py`/`radix_cache.py` in different spots (trivial rebase if stacked); #28510's `cache_match` event correlates with #28509's routing span via `trace_id` but works standalone.

I re-tested this on top of the latest `main` and everything works as expected. Setup: an SGLang deployment serving an FP8 model with hierarchical cache enabled (L1 GPU + L2 host) behind the cache-aware router (2 workers). I merged #28507, #28508, #28510 (engine) together with #28509 (router) onto the current `main`, rebuilt the images, and drove mixed traffic — repeated shared-prefix prompts to force cache hits plus a large number of distinct long prompts to force L1/L2 eviction — then scraped the metrics through Prometheus/Grafana. All the new metrics are emitted and populated with sane values: - Engine (`sglang:` prefix): cache_entry_count, cache_total_tokens, evicted_tokens_total, cache_eviction_events_total, cache_eviction_age_seconds (histogram), cache_eviction_reuses (histogram), hicache_host_evicted_tokens_total, hicache_host_eviction_age_seconds (histogram). - Router cache-aware decision metrics: the policy-branch counter(cache_hit / cache_miss_min_load / ...), the match-rate summary, and the per-worker tree-size gauge. Everything flowed into Prometheus and rendered correctly across all the corresponding Grafana panels (eviction lifetime/frequency, radix cache footprint/capacity, and gateway cache-aware decisions). No issues observed.

Thanks @chenkaiyue. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces cache lifetime and eviction-age observability metrics for both L1 (GPU) and L2 (host/CPU DRAM) caches, adding new Prometheus histograms and counters to track eviction age, idle time, reuse counts, and eviction events. The review feedback suggests ensuring that these metrics are recorded only after successful eviction operations in both `hiradix_cache.py` and `radix_cache.py` to avoid inaccurate metrics in case of failures.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In `evict_host`, the eviction age metric is observed before the eviction operation is actually performed. If `self.cache_controller.evict_host` raises an exception or returns `0` (meaning no tokens were actually evicted), the recorded metric will be inaccurate. It is safer and more accurate to observe the age and increment the tokens only after a successful eviction (i.e., when `host_evicted > 0`).

In `evict_host`, the eviction age metric is observed before the eviction operation is actually performed. If `self.cache_controller.evict_host` raises an exception or returns `0` (meaning no tokens were actually evicted), the recorded metric will be inaccurate. It is safer and more accurate to observe the age and increment the tokens only after a successful eviction (i.e., when `host_evicted > 0`).

issue_comments.body:
Cache-observability series (independent, any merge order):
- #28509 `[router]` cache-aware decision observability (gateway/Rust)
- #28507 `[metrics]` cache eviction lifetime/frequency L1+L2 (engine)
- #28508 `[metrics]` radix cache size gauges (engine)
- #28510 `[tracing]` per-request cache-match snapshot (engine)

Only coupling: #28507 and #28508 edit `metrics_collector.py`/`radix_cache.py` in different spots (trivial rebase if stacked); #28510's `cache_match` event correlates with #28509's routing span via `trace_id` but works standalone.

I re-tested this on top of the latest `main` and everything works as expected. Setup: an SGLang deployment serving an FP8 model with hierarchical cache enabled (L1 GPU + L2 host) behind the cache-aware router (2 workers). I merged #28507, #28508, #28510 (engine) together with #28509 (router) onto the current `main`, rebuilt the images, and drove mixed traffic — repeated shared-prefix prompts to force cache hits plus a large number of distinct long prompts to force L1/L2 eviction — then scraped the metrics through Prometheus/Grafana. All the new metrics are emitted and populated with sane values: - Engine (`sglang:` prefix): cache_entry_count, cache_total_tokens, evicted_tokens_total, cache_eviction_events_total, cache_eviction_age_seconds (histogram), cache_eviction_reuses (histogram), hicache_host_evicted_tokens_total, hicache_host_eviction_age_seconds (histogram). - Router cache-aware decision metrics: the policy-branch counter(cache_hit / cache_miss_min_load / ...), the match-rate summary, and the per-worker tree-size gauge. Everything flowed into Prometheus and rendered correctly across all the corresponding Grafana panels (eviction lifetime/frequency, radix cache footprint/capacity, and gateway cache-aware decisions). No issues observed.

Thanks @chenkaiyue. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces cache lifetime and eviction-age observability metrics for both L1 (GPU) and L2 (host/CPU DRAM) caches, adding new Prometheus histograms and counters to track eviction age, idle time, reuse counts, and eviction events. The review feedback suggests ensuring that these metrics are recorded only after successful eviction operations in both `hiradix_cache.py` and `radix_cache.py` to avoid inaccurate metrics in case of failures.
